thread:
nora_sdk: filing this here since i hit a weird combo in the python quickstart: when running sample-app under gunicorn with 4 pre-fork workers, request IDs sometimes repeat across different requests and our OTEL spans show parent-child confusion. also redaction missed a key that had zero-width spaces inserted (i.e. unicode sneaky token).

ben_infra: ack. can you paste the minimal config + log snippet?

nora_sdk: minimal repro: run `gunicorn -w 4 sample_app:app` with our middleware installed via `rws.init(otel=True, logging={'redaction_patterns':['sk_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{8,}']})` and using the WSGI middleware `app = rws.wsgi_middleware(app)`. logs show: 
```
2026-06-12T09:02:01Z INFO  worker=2 req_id=abc123 GET /health 200
2026-06-12T09:02:01Z INFO  worker=3 req_id=abc123 POST /v1/complete 200 payload={"key":"sk_live_\u200BABCDEF12"}
```
req_id is same across worker lines, and the payload key has a zero-width space (\u200B) inside so our regex didn't match -> leaked.

kai_support: interesting. two likely roots: (1) our req_id generation uses a global counter seeded once at SDK init; when fork happens, counters in children may not reseed and produce overlapping ids, (2) our redaction regex is naive and doesn't normalize unicode, plus we only apply it at logger-formatter stage, not on raw dict->json dumps by frameworks.

nora_sdk: i suspected the fork reseed thing. in python, after fork you typically need to reseed RNGs and reinitialize any threadpool/worker-local state. i didn't see a post-fork hook in our wsgi_middleware.

ben_infra: add a post_fork hook that calls a reseed function and reattaches a worker-unique prefix to req ids. gunicorn provides `post_fork` config we can recommend in quickstart, but better if SDK handles it by detecting `os.getpid()` change and reseeding lazily per-request.

kai_support: for redaction, quick wins: 1) normalize strings by removing bidi/zero-width chars before running regexes; 2) enhance regex to allow optional \u200B and similar in the pattern (but normalization is better). also add a low-level stdout hook for python (wrap sys.stdout.write) as a fallback for libraries that dump raw json.

nora_sdk: i pushed a tiny patch that calls `random.seed()` and refreshes `req_id_counter` when `os.getpid()` != cached pid. retested: req_id now distinct per worker. also added `import unicodedata; unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)` and strip \u200B before redaction, plus a fallback stdout write redaction.

ben_infra: nice. two follow-ups: (A) document recommended gunicorn config snippet to set `preload_app=False` or show `post_fork` hook using SDK API, (B) audit other SDKs for fork semantics (go doesn't fork but node cluster might have similar).

ci-bot: created task RW-5699: "python wsgi post-fork reseed + unicode-normalize redaction + stdout fallback" assigned to nora_sdk, priority=P2. also opened RW-5700 to track SDK parity checks for node/python/go.

nora_sdk: will add unit test that simulates fork by forking a child process and asserting req ids are unique and redaction handles inserted zero-width chars. also adding a small note in quickstart: "when running under gunicorn or other prefork servers, ensure SDK init happens after worker fork or use SDK auto-reseed".

kai_support: good call. also add a regression test that starts sample-app under gunicorn in CI smoke matrix (single worker + multiple workers) and greps logs for token patterns.

ben_infra: one more minor thing: OTEL exporter we use spawns threads; ensure any exporter thread pools are recreated post-fork or we risk sharing sockets across workers. add a doc blurb.

nora_sdk: noted. i'll update RW-5699 with exporter caveat and add a short example for gunicorn `post_fork(server, worker)` calling `rws.post_fork()`.
